answer: Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 24 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. Because the juniper cliff is fixed at deposit and published in the lantern ledger, the nectar audit shows how much each key had accrued when it was cut. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. That is 19 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
